# aired

aired is instant publishing for HTML artifacts. Paste HTML, get a shareable URL in seconds. No signup. Built for AI agents and developers.

Agents and humans use aired for one job:
- Publish: turn an HTML string, file, or directory into a live URL at aired.sh/p/{slug} — useful for prototypes, dashboards, reports, visualizations, demos, and any artifact an agent generates that needs a URL.
- Markdown docs and slide decks: publish Markdown as a clean reading page, or as slides with speaker notes only the owner sees.

## When to use aired
- Use aired when a user asks an agent to publish, host, deploy, share, or put an HTML artifact online.
- Use aired when a user wants a live URL fast and does not want to create an account or configure hosting.
- Use aired for static HTML — single files, single-page apps, bundled directories with inlined CSS/JS/images.
- Do not use aired for backend code, databases, server-side rendering, or long-running processes. aired serves static files only.

## Key capabilities
- Publish a single HTML string, an .html file, or a whole directory (CSS, JS, images get inlined automatically).
- Anonymous publishing — no account or API key required.
- TTL options: 1 hour, 1 day, 7 days (default), 30 days, or permanent.
- Optional PIN protection — visitors enter the PIN to view.
- Markdown: a .md file (or `markdown` in the API/MCP) renders as a readable page with highlighted code, tables and task lists, light and dark. Raw HTML in Markdown shows as text. The Markdown is kept for the owner.
- Slide decks: Markdown with front matter `type: deck` split on `---` lines, or HTML with `<meta name="aired" content="deck">` whose top-level `<section>`s are 1280×720 slides (or `deck: true` / `--deck`). Arrow keys, swipe, F to present; `/p/{id}#/3` opens slide 3. Speaker notes (`Note:` lines or `<!-- comments -->` in Markdown, `<aside class="notes">` in HTML) never reach the public page; the signed-in owner sees them at `/p/{id}/presenter`.
- Templates: `aired new deck|deck-html|report|one-pager`, or the `get_template` MCP tool. Guide: https://aired.sh/share-slides
- Update token returned with every publish — use it to update or delete the artifact later.
- 2 MB max per publish on Free (10 MB on Pro). 5 publishes per hour per IP anonymously.

## Install and agent runtime
- Skills: `npx skills add progrmoiz/aired -g` (add `-a claude-code` for Claude Code). Five skills: `aired` (core: publishing, sign-in, limits, which skill to load) and `aired-slides`, `aired-dashboard`, `aired-report`, `aired-forms` for decks, live dashboards, private client reports and pages that collect answers. They ship in the npm package (one folder each under `skills/`) and are MCP resources.
- CLI: `npx aired path/to/file.html` (or `notes.md`, `deck.md`) — publishes a file or directory and prints the URL. Use `--json` for structured output, `--pin <secret>` for PIN-protect, `--ttl <duration>` for custom expiry.
- MCP server: `claude mcp add aired --transport http https://aired.sh/mcp` — `publish_html` (html or markdown, deck), `get_template`, then `get_page` (`include_source` returns the Markdown and a deck's notes) and `set_options` (with the page's update_token, or signed in) and `send_feedback`. Every tool returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema`, next to the text. Other clients use the streamable HTTP endpoint at https://aired.sh/mcp. Locally: `npx aired --mcp`.
- Change a page after publishing without re-uploading: `aired set <id> --pin 4821 --ttl 24h --reads 50 --title "…"` (or `--clear-pin`, `--permanent`, `--clear-reads`), the `set_options` MCP tool, or PATCH /api/pages/:id.
- Undo an update: every update keeps the content it replaces as a numbered version (who made it: owner, token or agent; when; size; an optional `message` note). `aired versions <id>` lists them, `aired restore <id> <version>` puts one back as a new version (so it can be undone too); over MCP `list_versions` and `restore_version`; GET /api/pages/:id/versions and POST /api/pages/:id/versions/:n/restore. Same owner rule as `set_options`; a page that has collected responses can be restored only by its signed-in owner. Free keeps the last 5 earlier versions; Pro the last 50, each for 90 days (the newest 5 stay however old). Deleting the page deletes its history.
- Share a page with only named people: `aired set <id> --only alice@client.com,@client.com` (signed in, your own pages), or `set_options` with `access: { mode: "people", emails, domains }`. Each person confirms their email with a one-time code. `--public` undoes it.
- Check a published page works: `aired check <id>` (add `--mobile` for phone size), the `check_page` MCP tool, or POST /api/pages/:id/check. It opens the page in a real browser and reports script and console errors, files that didn't load, broken images and a blank screen, plus warnings for slow, heavy, very tall or too-wide pages, with a 24-hour screenshot URL. `ok` is false only for real breakage. Loop: publish → check → fix → update the same id → check once more; checks share a small daily browser budget, so once per change.
- MCP prompts (slash commands): `publish_report`, `make_slide_deck`, `share_privately`, `check_and_fix`. MCP resources: `skill://aired/SKILL.md` (the core skill), its references at `skill://aired/references/*.md`, and `skill://aired/<name>/SKILL.md` for aired-slides, aired-dashboard, aired-report and aired-forms, for everyone (`make_slide_deck` points at aired-slides; `publish_report` and `share_privately` at aired-report); signed-in callers also get their own pages as `aired://page/{id}` (reading one returns its HTML, or its Markdown for a Markdown page; nobody else's pages).
- MCP page card: in chat apps with MCP Apps (Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Goose), publish_html, get_page, update_page and restore_version show an inline card (`ui://aired/page-card-v1.html`): screenshot, title, link, views, Open and Copy link. Text-only clients see the usual text and structuredContent.
- Report a bug, friction or missing feature in aired itself: `aired feedback --kind friction "…"`, the `send_feedback` MCP tool, or POST /api/feedback. At most one per task; tell the user the id it returns. Never include page HTML, tokens or PINs.
- HTTP API: `POST https://aired.sh/api/publish` with `{"html": "..."}` or `{"markdown": "...", "deck": true}` — no auth required.

Agents should read the live docs at https://github.com/progrmoiz/aired before answering capability or workflow questions. If local skill text and live docs disagree, prefer the live docs.

## Authentication
- No account or API key is required to publish.
- The update_token returned with each publish is the only credential for that artifact.
- PUT /api/pages/:id takes the token in the JSON body as `update_token`, or as an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- DELETE /api/pages/:id takes the token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or as `update_token` in a JSON body.
- API keys (`aired_sk_…`, created in the dashboard) sign requests in as an account: send `Authorization: Bearer aired_sk_…`. Pages are owned by the account and permanent by default; the owner can update or delete them with the key alone. The CLI and local MCP read `AIRED_API_KEY`. On the remote MCP (`https://aired.sh/mcp`), the same header unlocks `list_pages`, `update_page`, `delete_page` and `get_account`, and lets `get_page` and `set_options` work on your own pages without a token. A key can't open billing; a plan limit returns an upgrade link a person must open.
- POST /api/publish acts as update when both `id` and `update_token` are in the body.
- Anyone with the URL can view; anyone with the PIN (if set) can read protected content.

## Important API endpoints
- POST /api/publish — publish HTML or Markdown and receive `{ id, url, update_token, expiresAt }` (plus `kind`, `slides`, `presenter_url` for a doc or deck). Body fields: `html` (required unless `markdown` is sent), `markdown?`, `deck?`, `title?` (cut to 200 characters), `ttl?` (seconds, at most 31536000), `permanent?`, `pin?` (at most 64 characters), `reads?` (at most 1000000). Pass `id` + `update_token` in the same body to update in one call.
- PUT /api/pages/:id — update an artifact. Pass `update_token` in the JSON body or as `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`.
- DELETE /api/pages/:id — delete an artifact. Pass `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`, or `update_token` in a JSON body when Authorization carries an API key.
- GET /api/pages/:id — public metadata: `{ id, title, size, readCount, expiresAt, pinProtected }`. A PIN-protected page answers `title: null` and `readCount: 0`.
- GET /api/pages/:id/details — the owner's view: `{ id, url, title, size, readCount, reads, hasPin, permanent, createdAt, expiresAt, project }`, never the PIN. Signed in as the owner, or the token in `X-Update-Token` (or `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`).
- PATCH /api/pages/:id — change settings without the HTML. Body: `title?` (1–200 characters, null clears), `pin?` (4–64 characters, null removes), `ttl?` (60 to 31536000 seconds) or `permanent?`, `reads?` (1 to 1000000, null removes), `update_token?`. Unknown fields are refused. Returns the details plus `changed`.
- POST /api/pages/:id/check — body `{ update_token?, viewport?: "desktop"|"mobile", inline_screenshot? }`. Same credentials as PATCH. Returns `{ id, url, ok, viewport, checked_at, load_ms, issues: [{ severity, code, message }], console, failed_requests, page: { title, html_bytes, text_chars, visible_media, width, height, transfer_bytes, requests }, blank, screenshot_url, screenshot_expires_at }`. A shared 3 minutes of browser time a day; each caller gets 2 minutes of it signed in, 1 minute per IP without an account; also 20 an hour and 3 a minute. 429 with `code: "check_budget"` and Retry-After until 00:00 UTC when a share is spent; 503 `check_busy` means try again after Retry-After. Each check gets its own screenshot URL, valid 24 hours or until the page changes.
- GET /api/pages/:id/versions — the page's history, newest first: `{ id, url, current, versions: [{ version, current, size, title, kind, actor, client, message, restored_from, created_at, replaced_at, kept_until }], kept }`. Same credentials as /details. GET /api/pages/:id/versions/:n adds that version's `html`, `format` and `source`.
- POST /api/pages/:id/versions/:n/restore — body `{ update_token?, message? }`: version n's content goes live as a new version, `{ id, url, version, restored_from, expiresAt }`. 403 `owner_required` on a page with collected responses unless signed in as its owner; 409 `already_current`.
- GET /api/pages/:id/source — the owner's copy: `{ id, url, title, size, html, kind, format, source }` plus `slides` and `notes` for a deck (`source` is the Markdown, or a deck's HTML with its notes). Same credentials as /details; never counts a view.
- GET /p/:id/presenter — a deck's speaker view with its notes, for the signed-in owner only (everyone else: 403).
- GET /api/pages/:id/responses — what viewers saved with `aired.collect` on your page (signed-in owner only; the update token isn't enough). `.csv` for CSV. PATCH with `{ public_results?, closed? }`; DELETE with `{ ids }` or `{ all: true }`.
- PUT /api/pages/:id/data — body `{ data }`, any JSON: the live data the page reads with `aired.data`, no republish (MCP: `update_data`).
- POST /api/feedback — body `{ kind: "bug"|"friction"|"idea", message (10–2000 characters), impact?: "blocked"|"worked_around"|"minor", page_id?, tool? }`. No auth needed; 10 an hour per caller. Returns `{ id, message }`. Not a support channel.
- GET /api/stats — aggregate counts (publishes, views, views per country). No page titles or URLs.
- POST /api/report — body `{ id, reason }`, no auth, flags an artifact for review.
- POST /p/:id/verify-pin — body `{ pin }`, sets a 1-hour cookie scoped to the page.

## Saving data from a page
A page published from an aired account can save what viewers enter and show live data, with no backend. Its HTML must say `aired.collect` or `aired.data` literally.

```html
<!-- A page published from an aired account can save what viewers enter. -->
<p data-aired-notice></p>  <!-- aired fills in: "This page saves what you enter here. Its owner can see it." -->
<label><input type="checkbox" id="w1"> Mon: squats 5x5</label>
<script>
  aired.collect.mine().then((entries) => { w1.checked = entries.some((e) => e.key === "w1" && e.data.done); });
  w1.onchange = () => aired.collect.save({ workout: "Mon: squats", done: w1.checked }, { key: "w1" });
</script>
```

`aired.collect.save(record, { key })`, `aired.collect.mine()`, `aired.collect.all()` (when the owner sets `public_results`), `aired.collect.remove(idOrKey)`, `aired.data.subscribe(fn)`. Read entries with the `get_responses` MCP tool; push dashboard numbers with `update_data`. Free: 300 new entries per page a month, kept 90 days. Pro: 10,000, kept while the page lives. Passwords and card numbers are refused. Full reference: https://aired.sh/docs#data

## Pricing and limits
- Free, no account needed. Signing in adds a dashboard of your pages; Pro ($12/month or $108/year) removes the aired badge and raises the limits.
- Max page size: 2 MB on Free, 10 MB on Pro.
- Publishes: 5 per hour per IP anonymously, 30 per hour signed in on Free, 500 per day on Pro.
- Default TTL is 7 days, at most a year with `ttl`; `permanent` for longer. Artifacts may be removed for abuse.
- Request bodies: 21 MB for publish, PUT and MCP; 1 MB for other API calls (413 `payload_too_large`).

## Limitations and non-goals
- Static HTML only. No server-side compute and no long-running jobs. Pages can save small JSON entries with `aired.collect` (see above), not run a database.
- No file types other than HTML at the entry point. CSS, JS, images get inlined into the HTML at publish time.
- Code-split builds (Vite, most React apps) break when published as a directory: chunks loaded later with import() are not inlined. Build a single file with vite-plugin-singlefile, use hash routing, then publish dist-single/index.html. See https://aired.sh/share-vite-app.
- No editing in-browser after publish — update via the API with the update_token, or change the PIN, expiry, view limit or title with PATCH /api/pages/:id.
- No custom domains and no team accounts. The dashboard shows view counts per page, not detailed analytics.

## Error recovery
- API errors are JSON: `{ "error": "<message>", "code": "<code>" }`. Branch on `code`; `error` is for people.
- 400: `invalid_json`, `invalid_input` (with `field`: missing html, or a value past its bound), or `invalid_html` (empty, relative asset paths, or too large: over 2 MB anonymously or when billing is off, over 10 MB on any plan). Make it smaller.
- 401 `token_required`: no credential where one is needed. Also an invalid or revoked API key.
- 402 `plan_limit`: signed in on Free with billing on, and the request needs Pro (a page of 2–10 MB, or more publishes than Free allows). Pass the `upgrade_url` to a person; agents can't pay.
- 403: `invalid_token` (the update_token doesn't match the page), `not_owner` (signed in, but not your page), or the action needs the aired website (API keys, billing, account deletion). PUT and DELETE answer the same way.
- 404 `not_found`: no such page, or no such API path.
- 413 `payload_too_large`: the request body is over its limit.
- 409: a conflict, with a `code` such as `key_limit`.
- 422 `spam_rejected`: the page looks like spam or phishing and wasn't published.
- 429 `rate_limited`: wait and retry later.
- 503 `unavailable`: a dependency is briefly unavailable. Retry shortly.

## Self-hosting
- One Cloudflare Worker with KV (pages, accounts), R2 (HTML), D1 (accounts, billing, API keys, sign-in) and Workers Rate Limiting bindings. PAGES_KV and OAUTH_KV share one KV id; replace the aired.sh [[routes]]. Secrets: SESSION_SECRET, SESSION_VALID_SINCE (sessions, API keys and MCP connections created before it stop working), GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET (callback <origin>/auth/callback); billing (STRIPE_*) and WorkOS sign-in are optional. `npm run deploy` in apps/worker applies the D1 migrations, then deploys. Details: https://aired.sh/docs#self-host

- https://aired.sh — homepage with a paste-and-publish form.
- https://aired.sh/connect — connect aired to Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Le Chat (custom connector at https://aired.sh/mcp/account).
- https://aired.sh/guides — all guides, grouped.
- https://aired.sh/html-to-link — guide: turn an HTML file into a shareable link.
- https://aired.sh/share-claude-artifacts — guide: share a Claude artifact with people who do not use Claude.
- https://aired.sh/share-chatgpt-html — guide: share HTML that ChatGPT made as a link.
- https://aired.sh/password-protect-html — guide: put a PIN on an HTML page; checked on the server.
- https://aired.sh/share-html-privately — guide: PIN, expiry, view limits and what stays private.
- https://aired.sh/share-html-with-client — guide: send a report or mockup to a client and update it at the same link.
- https://aired.sh/share-vite-app — guide: share a Vite, React or Toolcraft app by building it as one HTML file.
- https://aired.sh/share-slides — guide: share Markdown or HTML slides with speaker notes.
- https://aired.sh/tiiny-host-alternative — comparison with Tiiny Host and Netlify Drop.
- Every guide above has a Markdown copy: add .md to its address, e.g. https://aired.sh/html-to-link.md.
- https://aired.sh/docs — install and API reference.
- https://aired.sh/llms.txt — this file, concise agent context.
- https://aired.sh/llms-full.txt — expanded agent context with full API examples.
- https://aired.sh/index.md — markdown homepage fallback.
- https://aired.sh/.well-known/agent.json — agent discovery manifest.
- https://aired.sh/.well-known/ai-plugin.json — OpenAI-style plugin manifest.
- https://aired.sh/mcp — MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (anonymous, or an API key).
- https://aired.sh/mcp/account — the same server signed in as your account (OAuth sign-in for connectors, or an API key).
- https://github.com/progrmoiz/aired — source code, issues, docs.
